The ceremony will take place at the Madison Municipal Building with speeches from local leaders. The event will emphasize the city's commitment to disability justice and inclusion. MADISON, Wis. — In order to commemorate the 35th anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act, the City of Madison will host a Disability Pride Flag Raising Ceremony on Tuesday afternoon. Community members are invited to attend this ceremony at 2:30 p.m. in front of the Madison Municipal Building, where the mayor, common council members, disability advocates, and others will be speaking. "Disability justice is community justice, and Madison must lead with both visibility and accountability,” said Alder Dina Nina Martinez-Rutherford. July is recognized as Disability Pride Month. The ceremony will honor the strength, resilience, and contributions of the disability community and highlight the city’s commitment to equity, inclusion, and accessibility for all residents. “Disability Pride Month is a time to honor the legacy of disability rights advocates and activists who made it possible for us to learn, work, travel, and participate in public life. It is also a time to celebrate our disabled identities, stand in solidarity with one another, and recommit ourselves to the many fights for access, inclusion, and equity that we continue to face today, said Disability Rights Services Specialist for the City of Madison, Rebecca Hoyt. American Sign Language interpretation will also be provided.  ​COPYRIGHT 2025 BY CHANNEL 3000. ALL RIGHTS RESERVED. THIS MATERIAL MAY NOT BE PUBLISHED, BROADCAST, REWRITTEN OR REDISTRIBUTED.
